extracted.intended_audience: GCC policymakers, national IP offices, IP professionals, and international partners (e.g., EU)
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and evaluative criteria for reforming and harmonizing intellectual property laws and policies across GCC member states, with attention to patent, trademark, copyright, GI, design regimes and institutional capacity building. Oriented toward policymakers and IP offices planning regional cooperation and legal reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public acceptance and balance between innovation incentives and public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising awareness among the population regarding the new system is keen but most importantly is the acceptance of the population of such changes. It is also important that a balance is found between incentivizing innovation and respecting the public interest and his right to access to information provided by this innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy reforms should not unduly restrict public access or social welfare. Use TRIPS flexibilities (e.g., IP & public health, IP & access to knowledge) where appropriate. Ensure reforms enable use of technological knowledge for social and economic welfare rather than creating barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess regulatory impact on innovation (Innovation Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a regulation is under consideration, its impact on innovation should be assessed and addressed (the “Innovation Principle”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design legislation to create the best possible conditions for innovation to flourish; promote an informed dialogue between industry, policymakers and other stakeholders; avoid rigid, detailed regulations that suppress innovation and competitiveness. See EU practice and the repository of industry cases on regulation impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design research & innovation programmes that couple R&I to economic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmes should drive economic growth and create jobs by coupling research and innovation (R&I), with emphasis on excellent science, industrial leadership and tackling societal challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Horizon 2020 lessons: support multi-disciplinary international networks, research infrastructures, training and mobility of researchers. Use programme design to produce world-class science while promoting industrial leadership and societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt competition-aware transfer-of-technology rules (EC TTBER model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the EC Regulation on Transfer of technology of 2014 (TTBER and Guidelines) as a model for assessing technology transfer agreements through which a licensor permits exploitation of patents, know-how or software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider adopting competition rules that balance licensing freedoms with competition policy; use EU guidelines as reference when drafting national/regional rules governing tech-transfer agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization should be tailored and gradual, not a straight EU transplant
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU model (unitary trademarks, unitary designs, harmonized copyright and patents, Unified Patent Court) is a good example, but GCC countries must tailor the process to their specific challenges and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the EU took decades to reach current harmonization; harmonization in GCC should consider local visions/strategies, capacity building, investments in education and R&D, and be receptive to public acceptance. Aim for rules tailored for GCC rather than wholesale adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified copyright law for the digital environment (first step)
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC countries should develop a unified copyright law that eliminates gaps between GCC copyright legislation and adopts measures to address the protection of copyright and related rights in the digital environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize a unified/regional instrument focused on digital copyright rather than immediately harmonizing traditional issues (e.g., term of protection). Create a task force with representatives from digital content industries, government, enforcement bodies, consumer protection organizations and IP associations to identify common rules and address deficiencies affecting the GCC Common Market. Avoid extending term of protection from 50 to 70 years at this stage as it would delay free access and impose additional costs on consumers while creative industries are still developing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a multi-stakeholder task force for digital copyright harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: A task force should be created to address deficiencies in national legislation relating to the protection of copyright in the digital age and their impact on the GCC Common Market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include representatives of digital content industries (authors, film producers, sound-recording producers, publishers, broadcasters, internet providers, telecom authorities/operators), relevant governmental institutions (ministries, enforcement bodies), consumer protection organizations, IP associations and other relevant parties. Objective: identify common rules/interests for protection in the digital GCC market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent filing routes post-GCC Unitary Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: With the end of the GCC Unitary Patent, applicants can use either the Paris Convention route (national filings with 12-month priority) or the PCT national phase route to protect patents in individual GCC Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess each national patent office's operational status (online filing, substantive examination, publishing, granting). Where national offices are not fully operational, consider delegation to regional office or cooperation mechanisms; build national capacities for substantive examination and patent grant processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider validation agreements with the EPO as an option
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC countries could consider signing a validation agreement with the European Patent Office so that European patents have legal effect in GCC countries via a two-phase validation procedure (regional centralized phase before EPO, national phase after grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation respects partner state sovereignty (national offices register and national courts decide validity/infringement). Benefits include reduced duplication of search/examination, increased financial resources and enhanced technical capacity. Be mindful of concerns about domination in specific technical fields and local capacity constraints; GCC Patent Office may oppose validation for capacity reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use work-sharing mechanisms to improve examination efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt work-sharing modalities such as Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH), PCT-PPH pilots, and SHARE to minimize duplication and accelerate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH: if first office finds claims patentable, second office may fast-track examination using positive results. PCT-PPH pilots enable acceleration in national phase based on bilateral agreements. SHARE: office of first filing conducts search and examination and shares findings with second office. These mechanisms can conserve resources and speed processes, but require bilateral/regional agreements and trust in counterpart offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCC Patent Office role: regional services and capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: The GCC Patent Office should leverage its expertise post-unitary patent to provide services to help implement national visions: harmonize laws, create databases, promote tech transfer, raise IP awareness, and build professional and judicial capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical actions include: harmonizing IP laws/policies regionally; establishing a regional inventions/patents database; promoting technology cooperation and transfer among GCC countries; raising public awareness on IP; launching regional projects on the role of patents in GCC markets; developing a regional professional body for patent agents; building capacity of judiciary and court experts on patent laws and procedures; providing training in patent drafting, litigation, commercialization and transfer; supporting SMEs on using IP to protect/market inventions and attract investment (EPO SME practice as example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark harmonization plus capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: While the GCC Trademark Law provides uniform trademark protection and harmonized examination process (if ratified), it does not offer a unitary registration system; registration still requires separate national filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonization must go beyond law text to harmonize competency and knowledge of trademark offices and courts. Build capacity of examiners and train judiciary in trademark cases. Implementing regulations (e.g., for GI certification/collective marks) must be issued. Address high official fees that hinder accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical Indications (GIs): adopt appropriate protection system and registry
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC should consider developing GI legislation and a GI registry to protect regional and national GI products; choose whether to protect GIs via sui generis systems or via collective/certification marks under trademark law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that scope may include agricultural and non-agricultural products (handicrafts); consider EU and French experience as references. Start with national strategies and pilot projects, then consider regional coordination. The Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement can be an alternative flexible route; prioritize cooperation with EU on Madrid Agreement for border enforcement if helpful. Conduct study visits and capacity-building exchanges sensitive to culture and Sharia.

rubrics_metrics.name: GIs definition, scope and international agreements alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure national GI definitions are in line with TRIPS (quality/reputation attributable to geographical origin) and decide membership/participation in international instruments appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where countries adopt sui generis systems, align definitions with TRIPS/PGI standards. Understand that joining the Lisbon Agreement may be impractical now; Geneva Act may provide flexibility. Use Paris Convention and TRIPS as baseline international obligations. Tailor international treaty engagement to national readiness and existing GI inventories.

rubrics_metrics.name: GIs enforcement and public-policy compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide enforcement measures (precautionary measures, fines, imprisonment) and ensure GI protections conform to Islamic Sharia, public order and morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement should be available ex-officio or at the request of interested parties; protection may be based on reciprocity for WTO members. Draft laws (e.g., Saudi draft) include opposition procedures, ten-year renewable terms, and enforcement provisions—these are useful templates to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize industrial designs law and pursue unified/unitary design protections
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC industrial design laws need improvement and modernization to respond to the digital environment; develop a unified law with the aim of harmonizing the system and paving the way for a unitary design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EU evaluation of design rules and modernization as basis for GCC working papers. Assess current system, identify conflicting areas, and define actions to modernize and harmonize design protection across GCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and coordinate regional IP training and research centre functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The GCC IP Training Centre should build capacity of private/public sectors and academics, conduct research, run awareness campaigns, and coordinate with national initiatives (complement, not compete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on training in GIs, industrial designs (e.g., fashion & jewellery), collective management organizations, traditional knowledge and folklore. Complement national centres (e.g., Saudi IP Academy). Conduct studies on harmonization means, help establish regional CMOs, regional GIs registry, and unified industrial design frameworks.
